cabin has crew aboard.#comment: 1 when a crew member other than the pilot is aboard, 0 when the pilot is alone. The seat tracker flags CREW_OUT_n (2 doctor, 3 copilot, 4 HEMS1, 5 HEMS2; 0 = the seat model is occupied) count the members shown in the cabin; the members walking outside as objects (hoist_crew, pax3: the paperwork at the hospital, the visit) are taken away from that number, because macros such as drop heli rescuer set the seat models of a crew that is not there. Works with the wav packs too (it does not need the Mission Companion). The rear crew lines of the cabin (cabin secured, ready to fly) are only said when this is 1.

heli rescuer drop farewell.#comment: After the heli rescuers left the helicopter (param count 1 or 2; Mission Companion only, a wav pack says nothing): the pilot thanks them (HRD.PLT), a rescuer answers (HRD.HRT, actor 12 Heli rescuer, by voice) and the pilot tells the heli rescue base how many were left and where (HRD.BASE.Q) and the base answers (HRD.BASE.A, external radio). The arguments are the number (1 or 2) and the place (H hospital, B base, M the meeting point), spoken by the pack words of {hr:0} and {place:1} (user request of 2026-10-16: the decision of where the heli rescuers are left is told to their base).

heli rescuer pickup count.#comment: How many heli rescuers the pick-up takes: 2 with three crew and the option SECOND_HR yes (second Heli Rescuers loaded in 3 crew configuration), 1 otherwise. The same rule as pick heli rescuer ground and pick heli rescuer hoist, read when called: the option can be changed during the flight.

heli rescuer place.#comment: What the pick-up point of the heli rescuers is, for the radio calls (user request of 2026-10-20, with the guidelines of the user for the mountain rescue rendezvous): hrp_kind A an alpine rescue station (OSM emergency=mountain_rescue within 120 m of the point), F a fire station (amenity=fire_station), S a sports field (the usual result of Query random heli rescuer), M a point chosen by the pilot on the map (customhelirescuer yes: a meeting point). hrp_name is the name token of the station for A and F, the text - otherwise. The two small queries run once for each request, in the thread of the request; a station that was not found stays at [0,0] (far from the point). The Mission Companion says it with {hrp:1} (the place) and {hrs:1} (who answers on the radio). Runtime PENDING: whether the name token is filled for every station.

heli rescuer pickup request.#comment: Radio calls when the pick-up of the heli rescuers starts (user request of 2026-10-16, the mountain rescue rendezvous of 2026-10-20): the dispatcher gives the rendezvous at the pick-up place (HRQ.DSP), the pilot calls the station that waits there and asks if it is ready for 1 or 2 rescuers (HRQ.PLT.Q) and the station answers (HRQ.BASE.A), the pilot briefs it on the mission by kind and number of injured (HRQ.BRF.ACC, SAR, TRF, ORG or INJ) and the station acknowledges (HRQ.BASE.OK). The arguments of every message are the number, the kind of the place (A alpine rescue station, F fire station, S sports field, M meeting point) and its name (heli rescuer place). The requested number is kept in hrq_n for heli rescuer pickup arrival. Mission Companion only (the actor 12 is the Heli rescuer voice of the program); the wav packs have no such lines.

heli rescuer pickup approach.#comment: About three minutes before the pick-up point (the distance covered in 3 minutes at the ground speed, between 1.2 and 9 km), the pilot calls the station with the minutes to go and asks for the state of the landing area and the station answers with the wind (HRQ.APR.PLT, HRQ.APR.A; user request of 2026-10-20, from the mountain rescue guidelines). Once for each request: it ends when the rescuers are aboard (HELIRESCUER_BOARDED above 0), with a new request (hrq_n null) or at MISSION_PHASE 8. The wind comes from voice weather class (degrees in tens, knots). Mission Companion only. param seq = the value of hrq_seq when it was called.

heli rescuer pickup recheck.#comment: Called when the option SECOND_HR is changed in the settings: when a pick-up request was made (hrq_n) and the number of rescuers changed, the pilot corrects it at once and the station answers (HRQ.COR.PLT, HRQ.COR.A) instead of waiting for the arrival. Mission Companion only.

heli rescuer pickup arrival.#comment: The helicopter reaches the meeting point of the heli rescuers (Mission Companion only): the pilot announces the arrival and the station answers (HRQ.ARR.PLT, HRQ.ARR.A); when the number changed since the request (the option SECOND_HR was changed with three crew, or the crew changed) the pilot corrects it and the station answers (HRQ.COR.PLT, HRQ.COR.A, with the new number). The place of the request (hrp_kind, hrp_name, hrq_arg0) comes from heli rescuer place. Nothing when there was no request.

ensure door.#comment: Opens or closes one door only when its state asks for it (user request of 2026-10-16, after the heli rescuer was lowered and the crew re-entered through a closed door, twice). Params door (pax_right, pax_left, cargo_left, cargo_right) and want (open or closed). The state is the aircraft LVAR of the door (SDK_DOOR_PAX_R, SDK_DOOR_CARGO_L, SDK_DOOR_CARGO_R: 0 closed, 1 open, an animation in between counts as already moving); pax_left has no known LVAR and is always commanded as before. Returns 1 when a command was issued, 2 when a closing was, 0 when nothing was needed, so that the caller can wait for the animation. Every command is written in the ground crew runtime trace (macro doors) with the state read, so that a snapshot shows what the doors did. The commands open_door and close_door are not known to be idempotent: asking them only when needed also covers a toggle.

ensure door trace.#comment: Diagnosis of ensure door: writes in the ground crew runtime trace (macro doors) the state of the door LVAR four seconds after the command, so that a snapshot shows whether the door really moved (169.55 logged only the state read before the command). Params door (pax_right, cargo_left, cargo_right) and want.

hr terrain evaluate.#comment: User request of 2026-10-21: with a heli rescuer the patient walks to the rear doors (ground ops hems patient on foot) only when the ground is uneven; on level ground the stretcher of the helicopter is used as in the original. The heli rescuer read the altitude (AALT, feet) of the object jolly at the four points he stops on (hr_alt_lup, rup, rdwn, ldwn). The ground is uneven (HR_TERRAIN_STEEP 1) when, for a pair of the four points, the difference of altitude is more than 2 m, or more than the difference that makes 25 degrees over the distance between the two points (tan 25 = 0.4663, which is the limit for points closer than 4.3 m), or when the altitude of the helicopter differs from the altitude of the patient (injured_human) by more than the difference that makes 25 degrees over their distance. Any pair is tested (it includes the highest against the lowest point). The values stay in hr_terrain_* for the debug page and the ground ops trace. Runtime PENDING (AALT of a walking object, the distance between two locations).

ground ops hems patient on foot.#comment: User request of 2026-10-20: with a heli rescuer on the scene (HELIRESCUER_BOARDED above 0) the patient reaches the rear doors on foot, as in the hoist return, and the empty stretcher of the helicopter is ejected: the patient object walks behind the helicopter through bearing 180 at 5 m to bearing 175 at 1.5 m, the operator waits in front of the stretcher (bearing 170, 1 m), the empty stretcher is ejected (H STRETCHER_NOPATIENT and STRETCHER_EJECT), the patient object is removed and the patient appears on the stretcher (H STRETCHER_PATIENT), the stretcher retracts, the operator steps back, closes the rear doors and goes aboard along the side of the helicopter. No move_object: the stretcher object of the original loading appeared behind the helicopter with a jump (flight of 2026-10-20, 22:17). Called by 3 crew ground ops (CREW 3) and by 4 or 5 crew ground ops (AMBUFAR 0, patient by us); returns 1 when the patient is loaded, 0 when the patient could not be prepared. Test tools/test-hems-patient-on-foot.js, runtime PENDING.

apply hoist crew lifescore impact.#comment: Impact on the person on the cable. The medic (pax3, hoist_crew) is member 2. The second operator that rides the hook of a second hoist (4 and 5 crew, hpax1, the person of PAX_1) is member 4; the copilot (member 3) is never on the cable (in 4 crew it moves to PAX_2 to run the winch while the second operator is lowered). A heli rescuer is the member after the regular crew: CREW + HELIRESCUER_BOARDED, from 4 to 5. HOIST_CABLE_MEMBER and HOIST_CABLE_OBJECT come from hoist down (or from the up macros). The optional floor param is the lowest LifeScore the impact may leave: an injury that is not fatal stays above the critical threshold of the crew emergency (10), so the shift can go on.

hoist cable fall position.#comment: Where somebody who leaves the cable appears: at the user aircraft, now. Called at the moment of each release, so two people that let go at different times appear at two places.

apply aircraft failure.#comment: One aircraft failure by code, restored from the original 0.997 failure engine (codes 1 to 28). Used by the random in-flight failure and by the crash tiers.

Critical failures (user rule of 2026-10-18): an engine fire (5, 6) or a damaged transmission (18, 19) obliges to stop the helicopter and to call a mayday: critical failure mayday aborts the ground operations, the dispatcher is told, the crew calls on the radio and the operation is terminated after the landing.

reset aircraft failures.#comment: Repairs the helicopter: clears every failure and persistent damage that the failure table and the crash tiers can set. Called at the start of a mission when a crew member was critical or dead in the previous one (CREW_DEATH_REPAIR_PENDING, read also after a manual restart) and by the RESET FAILURES button of the Helicopter failures bar. It does not touch L:FAILURE, the random failure draw of the mission (the failure engine keeps working with it).

refresh aircraft failures flag.#comment: FAILURES_ACTIVE 1 when any failure or persistent damage that reset aircraft failures clears is present (engine failed or on fire, FADEC, hydraulics, fuel, autopilot, backup, APCP, MGB chip, T/MGB, MGB and engine damage, the fuel leakage). Read by the RESET FAILURES button of the Helicopter failures bar, which stays inactive while it is 0. L:FAILURE is not read: it holds the draw of a failure not yet occurred. Called when the settings are opened, after every failure and after every reset.

crash random failures.#comment: Random aircraft failures caused by a crash tier, drawn from the severity ladder (apply ladder failure) between the levels first and last: the severe tier (50 ft/s) from the lightest failure (APCP) to the engine failure (levels 1 to 10, no engine fire), the two highest tiers (90 ft/s and the catastrophic one) from the fuel failures to the engine fire (levels 7 to 11). Needs the failure setting ENGINE_FAILURES_ENABLED to be yes.

aircraft failure ladder.#comment: Severity ladder of the aircraft failures, from the lightest to the heaviest: 1 APCP (codes 14, 25), 2 autopilot 1/2 and the eight SEMA failures (11, 12, 22, 23 and 30 to 37), 3 MGB chip (15, 26), 4 FADEC 1/2 level 1 (3, 4), 5 backup (13, 24), 6 FADEC 1/2 level 2 (16, 17, 27, 28), 7 fuel (9, 10, 20, 21, the main and the two supply failures 38 to 40, and 29, the fuel leakage), 8 hydraulic (7, 8), 9 T/MGB mechanical damage (18, 19), 10 engine failed (1, 2), 11 engine fire (5, 6). The codes are the ones of apply aircraft failure (the original 0.997 codes 1 to 28 unchanged, 29 the fuel leakage, 30 to 40 the SEMA and fuel failures added later; the in-flight failure engine still draws only 1 to 28); the duplicates 20 to 28 stay with their level. Sets ladder_code from the param level with an equal chance for every code of the level, except level 2: its ten failures (autopilot 1, autopilot 2 and the eight SEMA) have the same chance each, and autopilot 1 and 2 then pick one of their two codes (11 or 22, 12 or 23).

apply ladder failure.#comment: One failure drawn from the severity ladder between the params first and last (levels 1 to 11, an equal chance for every level, then for every code of the level) and applied: the fuel leakage (code 29) by its own macro, every other code by apply aircraft failure.

fuel leakage.#comment: Fuel leakage: a constant amount, drawn once between 0.2 and 0.8 kg, is lost every 5 seconds (at most 0.8 x 12 = 9.6 kg per minute, never more than 10). The loss is taken from the center tank level in proportion to the total fuel weight (FUEL TOTAL QUANTITY WEIGHT, kg), so it adds to the other writers of the level (refuelling, the teleport loss) instead of overwriting them. Started once (fuel_leak_active), it ends with the fuel or when reset aircraft failures clears the flag.
